issues.legal_issue: Transfers made before the statutory reference date are outside the operation of the land-ceiling provisions.
material_facts: The land transfers at issue were made in 1956, before the statutory reference date.
The Commissioner included land transferred by the adopted son to his mother when calculating the appellant’s landholding.
issues.conclusion: The pre-reference-date transfers were outside the Act’s operation and the land transferred by the adopted son could not be included on that basis; the Commissioner’s order was set aside and the Deputy Collector’s order restored.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 8, 10 and 12 of the Maharashtra Agricultural Lands (Ceiling of Holdings) Act, 1961, provide that only transfers made on or after 4 August 1959 are affected by the Act. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: An authority is determining landholdings for the purpose of applying a ceiling on agricultural land.
predicates.transfers_precede_operative_cutoff: The transfers relied on to exclude land from the holding occurred before the statutory reference date.

issues.definition: When a land-ceiling proceeding concerns transfers made before the operative cutoff, those transfers are excluded from the ceiling computation.

issues.legal_issue: Separate individual property of a family member is not included in the landholding attributed to another owner or to the family as a unit.
material_facts: The adopted son transferred land to his mother under a civil court decree.
The Commissioner included that land in calculating the appellant’s landholding.
The land was treated as the mother’s personal property, rather than property belonging to the appellant or held as shared family property.
issues.conclusion: The mother’s separate property could not be clubbed with the appellant’s landholding or treated as land of the appellant’s family unit for the ceiling calculation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(11) and 2(22) define family and person, and section 6 addresses the holding of a family unit. The Court held that these provisions do not bring a family member’s separate or individual self-acquired property into the holding of the owner or family unit. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: An authority is determining landholdings for the purpose of applying a ceiling on agricultural land.
predicates.property_belongs_separately_to_family_me: The land is the separate individual property of a family member and does not belong to the owner or family as shared property.

issues.definition: In a land-ceiling proceeding, land that belongs separately to a family member is excluded from the ceiling holding attributed to the owner or family unit.

issues.legal_issue: A transfer cannot be treated as collusive or fraudulent without a basis in the pleadings or evidence.
material_facts: The transfers to the adopted son and from him to his mother occurred in 1956.
No pleading or case before the land authorities alleged that those transfers were collusive or fraudulent.
No evidence supported treating the transfers as collusive or fraudulent.
The High Court nevertheless presumed that the transfers and the decree were collusive.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in presuming collusion or fraud, because neither the pleadings nor the evidence supported that finding.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a finding or presumption of collusion or fraud must have a foundation in the pleadings or evidence; it relied on no statutory provision or earlier case for this point.

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: An authority is determining landholdings for the purpose of applying a ceiling on agricultural land.
predicates.transfers_challenged_as_collusive_or_fra: A party or reviewing court seeks to treat land transfers as collusive or fraudulent.
predicates.supporting_pleadings_or_evidence: The pleadings or evidence provide a factual basis for treating the transfers as collusive or fraudulent.

issues.definition: In a land-ceiling proceeding, transfers challenged as collusive or fraudulent are not treated that way when the pleadings and evidence provide no supporting basis.
